key_insight: HVOF WC-17Co coatings retain their best dry sliding wear performance at 200–400 °C, with a peak at 400 °C due to a protective tribo-oxide layer and compacted debris.
engineering_relevance: This suggests WC-17Co HVOF coatings can be used in moderately high-temperature wear environments, but performance degrades sharply above 400 °C as oxidation and binder damage accelerate.
method: HVOF-deposited WC-17Co coating tested in dry sliding wear from room temperature to 600 °C
Pre- and post-test characterization by SEM, EDS, XRD, and 3D surface profilometry
Wear tracked under constant load, sliding speed, duration, and distance
evidence_signal: The coating showed ~268.99 µm thickness, 1.53% porosity, 10.2 µm average surface roughness, and the lowest wear/friction at 400 °C.
watch_item: The improved wear window is temperature-limited; above 400 °C, oxide-layer breakdown and Co binder degradation can rapidly increase wear.
paper_title: Effect of thermal exposure on the wear and phase stability of HVOF-deposited WC-17Co coatings
